name: Google Business Profile Auto-Poster

parameters.content:
## Google Business Profile Auto-Poster

### How it works

1. Once a week, reads the firm's own Content Queue Google Sheet and finds the next row that hasn't been drafted yet.
2. Sends that raw content (a field note, tip, or announcement the firm typed in) to Claude to be repurposed into a single ready-to-paste Google Business Profile post — marketing copy only, same compliance rules as the Content Repurposer (PAC-31).
3. An independent post-hoc keyword scan re-checks the generated post for legal-sounding language before it's allowed through.
4. If it passes, the finished post text is emailed to staff to paste into Google Business Profile directly — this template does not call Google's Business Profile API to auto-publish. Direct posting access requires Google's own developer allowlist approval, which is a real barrier in practice (confirmed against this catalog's own Negative-Review Rapid Response template, PAC-50, whose Zapier-bridge approach to the same API has been stuck in Zapier's own account-approval queue) — so this template stays reliable for every firm by keeping a human as the one who clicks publish, rather than depending on access that may never come through.
5. The queue row is marked accordingly, the event is logged to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet, and staff get an email with the ready-to-paste post, or a flag if something needs a human look.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Create a Google Sheet named 'Content Queue' with columns: content, status, practice_area, posted_at, notes. Add a header row, then one row per post idea (leave status blank).
- [ ] Set GBP_CONTENT_QUEUE_SHEET_ID to that sheet's ID and connect the Google Sheets credential.
- [ ] Get an Anthropic API key from console.anthropic.com and connect it as a Header Auth credential (reuse from PAC-31/PAC-50 if already deployed).
- [ ] Set FIRM_NAME, FIRM_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, FIRM_STAFF_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID, and optionally FIRM_GBP_CTA_URL / FIRM_GBP_CTA_TYPE / FIRM_GBP_DASHBOARD_URL (reuse PAC-50's value if already deployed).
- [ ] Connect the SMTP credential.

### Customization

Adjust the weekly cadence on the trigger node. Edit the compliance rules or character limit directly in 'Build GBP Post Prompt' if your bar's advertising rules require different footer language. If your firm later gets approved Business Profile API access (directly or through Zapier), swap the final email step for a publish call — everything upstream of it (generation, safety check, queue tracking) stays the same.

## Trigger and content queue

Runs weekly, reads the firm's Content Queue sheet, and finds the next row that hasn't been drafted or flagged yet. If nothing's queued, staff get a reminder instead of the week going by silently empty.

## Generate and safety-check the post

Repurposes the raw content into one Google Business Profile post via Claude, then re-checks it with an independent keyword scan before anything is allowed through — same two-layer approach as PAC-31 and PAC-50.

## Draft delivery path

Emails the approved, ready-to-paste post straight to staff — this template doesn't call the Business Profile API to auto-publish (see the main note for why), so a human still clicks publish. Marks the queue row drafted and logs it either way.

## Flagged path

If either safety layer catches legal-sounding language, nothing is published. The queue row is marked 'Needs Review' so next week's run moves on to the next row instead of retrying the same one forever, and staff get the original content to fix or replace.

nodes.name: Weekly GBP Post Trigger
nodes.notes:
Fires once a week, Monday at 9am (n8n server timezone). Change the cron expression to post on a different day or more/less often — a solid local-SEO cadence is anywhere from weekly to twice a week.

This is the only thing that starts a run.

nodes.name: Fetch Content Queue Sheet
nodes.notes:
Reads every row from the firm's Content Queue sheet — expected columns: content, status, practice_area (optional), posted_at, notes.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'Google Sheets OAuth2' → connect the Google account that owns the sheet → save as 'Google Sheets account' (same credential name the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) uses — reuse it if already deployed).

Each returned row includes n8n's own row_number field (1-based, includes the header row) — used later to update this exact row without needing a separate ID column, same technique NTC-33 uses to target opt-out rows for deletion.

nodes.name: Find Next Queued Content Row
nodes.notes: Scans the sheet for the next actionable row. If every row is already 'Drafted', already 'Needs Review', or the sheet is empty beyond the header, has_content comes back false and the run ends with a reminder to staff instead of silently doing nothing.

nodes.name: If Has Queued Content
nodes.notes:
Yes (a queued row was found) → generate and publish this week's post.
No (queue is empty or exhausted) → remind staff to add more content rather than let the week pass with nothing posted.

parameters.text:
The Google Business Profile Auto-Poster ran today but found no queued content — every row in the Content Queue sheet is already marked Posted or Needs Review, or the sheet has no rows beyond the header.

Add a new row with a field note, tip, or announcement in the 'content' column (leave 'status' blank) so next week's run has something to work with.
parameters.subject: Google Business Profile queue is empty — nothing posted this week

nodes.name: Notify Staff Queue Empty
nodes.notes:
Heads-up email so an empty content queue is visible instead of the profile just quietly going stale.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: Build GBP Post Prompt
nodes.notes:
Builds the Claude prompt from this week's queued row. Same compliance rules as the Content Repurposer (PAC-31) — marketing copy only, no client-identifying details — trimmed to a single Google Business Profile asset with its actual 1,500-character hard limit.

Model: claude-sonnet-4-6. To reduce cost at the expense of quality, change to 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'.

nodes.name: Generate GBP Post Copy
nodes.notes:
Sends the prompt to Claude (Anthropic) and receives the post text as JSON.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'Header Auth' → Name: 'Anthropic API key' → Header Name: 'x-api-key' → Header Value: your key from console.anthropic.com. Reuse the same credential as PAC-31/PAC-50 if already deployed.

Cost: roughly $0.01-0.02 per run at ~800 output tokens — a weekly post costs under a dollar a year in AI spend.

nodes.name: Extract & Safety-Check GBP Post
nodes.notes:
Two-layer safety check, same pattern as PAC-31 and PAC-50: Claude's own self-report is Layer 1, an independent keyword regex scan is Layer 2. is_marketing_safe is only true if both pass.

Also enforces Google Business Profile's real 1,500-character limit — truncates at a word boundary and flags it in the summary rather than handing staff an over-length post to paste.

FIRM_GBP_DASHBOARD_URL is optional (reuse PAC-50's value if already deployed) — falls back to plain instructions if unset.

nodes.name: If Marketing Safe
nodes.notes:
Yes (both safety layers passed) → email the ready-to-paste post to staff.
No (Claude self-flagged, or the post-hoc scan caught legal-sounding language) → mark the row for human review instead.

nodes.name: Mark Queue Row As Drafted
nodes.notes:
Marks this row Drafted so next week's run moves on to the next queued row instead of regenerating the same content. 'Drafted' rather than 'Posted' since this template hands staff a ready-to-paste post rather than publishing it directly — see the main sticky note for why (Google restricts direct/bridged Business Profile posting access, and this catalog's own PAC-50 hit that wall via Zapier).

Matches on row_number (from the original read, 1-based including the header row) rather than a separate ID column — same technique NTC-33 uses to target a specific opt-out row. Verify the 'Column to Match On' dropdown shows row_number after import; reconfigure it in the UI if your n8n version labels it differently.

Same 'Google Sheets account' credential as the read step.

nodes.name: Log Draft To Compliance
nodes.notes:
Logs the generated draft to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet via the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33). This is internal record-keeping, not a message to a client — opt-out checking doesn't apply here.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

nodes.name: Notify Staff GBP Post Ready To Paste
nodes.notes:
Delivers this week's ready-to-paste post to staff — someone still needs to log into Google Business Profile and paste it in (30 seconds), since this template doesn't hold API access to publish automatically.

Credential: same 'Email account (SMTP)' credential as the queue-empty notification.

nodes.name: Mark Queue Row Needs Review
nodes.notes:
Marks this row 'Needs Review' with the safety-check's reason in the notes column — keeps it out of next week's pick without deleting it. A staff member can edit the content and reset status to blank to send it through again.

Same 'Google Sheets account' credential as the read step.

nodes.name: Log Flagged Content To Compliance
nodes.notes: Logs the exception to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet — every week's content is accounted for, whether published or flagged.

nodes.name: Notify Staff Content Flagged
nodes.notes:
Delivers the original content and the flag reason so staff can fix or replace the queue row themselves.

Credential: same 'Email account (SMTP)' credential as the other notifications.

json.content: We helped a client renegotiate a commercial lease after a landlord dispute over maintenance responsibilities — reminder that most lease issues can be resolved without going to court if you address them early.
Reminder: if you're starting a custody modification, bring your current parenting plan and any documentation of changed circumstances to your first consultation — it speeds up the whole process.

main.node: Notify Staff GBP Post Ready To Paste

description: Repurposes the firm's own field notes and content ideas into a weekly, ready-to-paste Google Business Profile post — Claude generates marketing-safe copy under the same compliance rules as the Content Repurposer (PAC-31), an independent keyword scan re-checks it, and the approved post is emailed straight to staff to paste in (direct/bridged API publishing access is unreliable to get from Google in practice). Flagged content is held for human review instead. Replaces a marketing retainer's local-SEO upkeep. Logs every draft and every exception to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet.
